{{short description|Molecular biologist, entrepreneur and community science advocate}}
{{about||the Danish historian and librarian|Ellen Jørgensen}}
'''Ellen D. Jorgensen'''<ref>{{cite web|title=Ellen D. Jorgensen|website=Bio Art, SVA NYC (bioart.sva.edu)|url=https://bioart.sva.edu/guest/ellen-d-jorgensen/}}</ref> (born 2 June 1955) is a New York-based [[Molecular biology|molecular biologist]] and serial entrepreneur. In addition to her long career in the biotechnology industry she is also credited with playing a leading role in promoting the [[do-it-yourself biology]] movement where she has worked to increase [[scientific literacy]] in the general population, particularly in the fields of molecular and [[synthetic biology]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.biosummit.org/ellen-jorgensen/|title=Ellen Jorgensen|website=Global Community Bio Summit|language=en-US|access-date=2018-03-30|archive-date=2018-06-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180619113147/https://www.biosummit.org/ellen-jorgensen/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite news|url=https://www.thnk.org/community/people/ellen-jorgensen/|title=Ellen Jorgensen- THNK School of Creative Leadership|work=THNK|access-date=2018-03-30|language=en-US}}</ref>  She is a co-founder of both non-profit ([https://biotechwithoutborders.org/ Biotech Without Borders]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Biotech Without Borders - HackerspaceWiki |url=https://wiki.hackerspaces.org/Biotech_Without_Borders |access-date=2024-09-09 |website=wiki.hackerspaces.org}}</ref> and [[Genspace]].<ref name=":0" /> ) and for-profit ([https://www.aanikabio.com/ Aanika Biosciences]<ref>{{Cite web |title=DLD Conference: Digital-Life-Design |url=https://dld-conference.com/speaker/ellen-jorgensen |access-date=2024-09-09 |website=dld-conference.com}}</ref>) biotechnology-based companies. In 2017, Ellen Jorgensen was named one of the Most Creative Leaders in Business by [[Fast Company (magazine)|Fast Company]].<ref name=":1" /> Her current focus is on combating climate change through her role as Vice President of Biotechnology at [https://carbonbridge.io/ CarbonBridge], a biotech startup that uses bacteria to remove environmental methane and create liquid fuel.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Carbon Bridge |url=https://indiebio.co/company/carbon-bridge/ |access-date=2024-09-09 |website=IndieBio - #1 in Early Stage Biotech |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Ellen Jorgensen graduated from [[New York University]] (NYU) in 1977 with a B.A. in [[Biology]]. She then went on to earn both her MA and MPhil in Biological Sciences from [[Columbia University]] in 1979 and 1981, respectively.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.linkedin.com/in/ellenjorgensen/|title=Ellen Jorgensen {{!}} LinkedIn|access-date=2017-03-27}}</ref> Jorgensen returned to NYU where she obtained her Ph.D. in [[Cell and molecular biology|Cell and Molecular Biology]] in 1987 from the [[Sackler Institute of Graduate Biomedical Sciences|Sackler Institute]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=http://www.onelab.org/people-jorgensen.html|title=ONE Lab|last=Aiolova|first=Maria|website=www.onelab.org|access-date=2018-03-30|archive-date=2019-04-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190402193305/http://www.onelab.org/people-jorgensen.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> She later went to [[SUNY Downstate College of Medicine|SUNY Downstate]] as a post-doc to continue research in [[protein structure]] and function.<ref name=":2" /> Jorgensen has served as adjunct faculty at [[Cooper Union|The Cooper Union]] in New York City,<ref name=":0" /> [[New York Medical College]] and at the [[School of Visual Arts]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ellen D. Jorgensen – SVA Bio Art Lab |url=https://bioart.sva.edu/guest/ellen-d-jorgensen/ |access-date=2024-09-09 |website=bioart.sva.edu}}</ref>

Jorgensen devoted many years of her career to various positions at both nonprofit and for-profit companies within the [[biotechnology]] sector.<ref name=":2" /> She spent eight years, from 2001 to 2009, as the Director of Biomarker Discovery and Development at Vector Research, researching early [[biomarker]]s of tobacco-related lung disease.<ref name=":2" /> In 2009, she co-founded the community [[Do-it-yourself biology|biohacker]] space, [[Genspace]]<ref name=":5">{{Cite news|url=https://www.ted.com/speakers/ellen_jorgensen|title=Ellen Jorgensen {{!}} Speaker {{!}} TED|last=Jorgensen|first=Ellen|access-date=2018-03-30|language=en}}</ref> where she developed innovative programming such as the [https://www.studentresearchnyc.org/our_programs/biorocket-internship-genspace/ Biorocket internships] for underserved New York City high school students and classes in genetic engineering for the general public. Under her leadership Genspace provided low-cost lab space for biotech entrepreneurs.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Techonomy |title=The New Biohackers: How (And Where) They Work |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/techonomy/2015/04/22/the-new-biohackers-how-and-where-they-work/ |access-date=2024-09-09 |website=Forbes |language=en}}</ref> [[Opentrons]] and [https://curieco.com/ Curieco] both used the Genspace pre-incubator space to launch successful companies. In 2017, Jorgensen founded Biotech Without Borders, a second nonprofit community biotechnology lab where she continues to serve on the board of directors.<ref name=":1" />

In 2009, Ellen Jorgensen co-founded [[Genspace]], the first nonprofit community biotech lab.  In 2010, Jorgensen initiated Genspace's curriculum of informal science education, leading to the company being named one the World's Top 10 Innovative Companies in Education.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":6" /><ref name=":7" />  The goal of Genspace is to increase scientific literacy in the general public by providing classes and workshops, as well as a space for community members to get involved in a biotechnology laboratory.<ref name=":4">{{Cite news|url=https://www.ted.com/talks/ellen_jorgensen_biohacking_you_can_do_it_too/transcript|title=Transcript of "Biohacking -- you can do it, too"|last=Jorgensen|first=Ellen|access-date=2018-03-30|language=en}}</ref> In March 2017, Ellen Jorgensen stepped down from her role as executive director to found Biotech Without Borders and was  replaced by Genspace co-founder, Daniel Grushkin.<ref name=":3">{{Cite news|url=https://technical.ly/brooklyn/2017/03/29/genspace-ellen-jorgensen-daniel-grushkin/|title=Ellen Jorgensen stepping down as head of Genspace, Daniel Grushkin to replace - Technical.ly Brooklyn|date=2017-03-29|work=Technical.ly Brooklyn|access-date=2018-03-30|language=en-US}}</ref> Jorgensen became [[Emeritus|president emeritus]].<ref name=":3" />

While Genspace was created with the goal of making scientific literacy more accessible, the organization was met with criticism by those that felt that hands-on science should be left to the professionals.<ref name=":4" />  Despite this criticism, Genspace has continued on, along with a larger community of hacker spaces opening worldwide, fostering an open environment of scientific collaboration and learning between amateurs and professionals.<ref name=":4" /><ref name=":5" />

Genspace is located in [[Brooklyn|Brooklyn, New York]].  The lab follows [[Biosafety level|Biosafety Level 1]] restrictions.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.genspace.org/the-lab/|title=About the Lab|website=Genspace|language=en-US|access-date=2018-03-30}}</ref>  Different membership tiers are offered providing access to events, classes, lab access, participation to community projects, and more.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.genspace.org/join-the-lab/|title=Join the Lab|website=Genspace|language=en-US|access-date=2018-03-30}}</ref>  In the spring of 2018, community projects will be offered in the fields of [[mycoremediation]], open plant collaboration, and [[optogenetics]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.genspace.org/community-projects/|title=Community Projects|website=Genspace|language=en-US|access-date=2018-03-30}}</ref>

=== Accolades ===
* World's Top 10 Innovative Companies in Education (Fast Company, 2014)<ref name=":7">{{Cite news|url=https://www.fastcompany.com/3026328/the-worlds-top-10-most-innovative-companies-in-education|title=The World's Top 10 Most Innovative Companies In Education|date=2014-02-13|work=Fast Company|access-date=2018-03-30|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":6">{{Cite web|url=https://www.genspace.org/support-us/|title=Support Us|website=Genspace|language=en-US|access-date=2018-03-30}}</ref>
* Maker Space of the Year (Brooklyn Innovation Awards, 2016 & 2017)<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://technical.ly/brooklyn/2017/01/06/brooklyn-innovation-awards-2016-winners/|title=Here's who won the Brooklyn Innovation Awards last night - Technical.ly Brooklyn|date=2017-01-06|work=Technical.ly Brooklyn|access-date=2018-03-30|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":6" /><ref name=":3"/>

== Biotech Without Borders ==
In 2017, Ellen Jorgensen stepped down from her leadership role at Genspace in order to found Biotech Without Borders, where she now acts as President.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" />  Biotech Without Borders is a Brooklyn, New York based [[Nonprofit organization|nonprofit]] public charity dedicated to enabling communities underrepresented in the biotechnology field to gain hands-on biotech lab experience.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.biotechwithoutborders.org/|title=About Us|website=Biotech Without Borders|language=en-US|access-date=2018-03-30}}</ref>  Biotech Without Borders focuses on providing a [[Biosafety level|Biosafety Level 2]] lab space, distributing biotech resources to labs worldwide, and engaging the public through hands-on lab classes, workshops, and events.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.biotechwithoutborders.org/our-mission-and-history|title=Our Mission And History|website=Biotech Without Borders|language=en-US|access-date=2018-03-30|archive-date=2019-01-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190119163918/https://www.biotechwithoutborders.org/our-mission-and-history|url-status=dead}}</ref>  It is the first Biosafety Level 2 lab open for public projects.  Compared to Genspace, Biotech Without Borders seeks to facilitate engagement with more authentic high-level science.
